observation: The whole set in the opening position, rebuilt after the colour-split repair. Front: the board is one thin slab and every piece stands on it, none floating and none sunk; the near rank reads as a size ladder, smallest globe to largest, on discs of one constant diameter, and the star's two flames are the only things taller than a piece. Top: the 7x9 grid is complete, sixteen worlds stand one to a cell with clear grey board visible all round every disc -- no two discs touch or overlap and none crosses a grid line; twelve belt tiles fill two three-by-two blocks either side of the centre file; three corona cells ring each star, cyan at the far end round the black plate and orange at the near end round the cream one; the two trays lie clear of the board. Iso: one coherent object, no missing or extra part, no visible intersection, no floating geometry. Earth's continents still read as continents at board scale on both armies, and nothing about any other world has moved: this packet is indistinguishable from the previous round's at every feature I can name, which is what the repair intended -- it changed which boolean answer is accepted, not what the set looks like. The top view carries no shading contrast on the tray wells and on the board's pockets because every surface it sees faces straight up; the front and iso views supply the depth evidence and resolve it.
